claims.text: The trip_record, the GPS trace and the fare breakdown all carry TRP-09112 and describe one continuous trip: the trace's first fix at 14:10:00 is the trip_record.started_at, its last fix at 14:32:00 is the trip_record.ended_at, and the ledger bills at 14:32:03. The rider has shown what POL-RD-08(a) requires — the artifacts describe the same trip.

The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes: 133 fixes at a 10-second sample interval, 100% coverage of the completed trip, no gaps, and a maximum gap of 0 seconds, so none of POL-RD-07 limbs (a) to (c) is engaged and no discount to the distances measured from it is warranted under POL-GEN-02. The measurement on this trip is the best evidence there is.

Under POL-RD-01 the governing figure is the trace, not the rounded convenience copy on the trip_record: the trace measures 11.5 km for the completed trip against a booked optimal of 10.0 km, an excess of 1.5 km driven and paid for. That excess clears the 0.8 km absolute limb of the establishment test.

The rider is straight about the arithmetic rather than stretching it: 1.5 km is 15% of the 10.0 km optimal, and POL-RD-01 requires the excess to exceed 20% of optimal AND 0.8 km absolute, both tests passing together. The percentage limb is not met on this record, and the rider does not assert that a route deviation is established by the 1.5 km excess.

Nothing on this record shifts the extra distance onto the rider. The trip's chat log holds exactly one message, sent by the RIDER at 14:21:40 — 'This looks a little longer than the route shown at booking' — which is a question, not an instruction: it names no road and no place, and waypoint_hint is null, so the corroboration test in POL-RD-04 cannot be run at all and the clause is unavailable. The driver's answer that he 'stayed on ordinary through roads and made no additional stop' points to no artifact and no clause, and under POL-RD-08 an assertion that cites no evidence ID carries no weight.

No traffic advisory covers this trip. The only advisory artifact in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-09112-01, is MISSING with weight 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT; the rider cites that absence, not any content, and discloses the weight as POL-GEN-02(1) requires. POL-RD-03 can therefore exonerate nothing here, because it demands an advisory naming a road the optimal route traverses within a validity window of the vehicle's passage.

Neither re-baselining route is open on this record. The trip_record shows no relocation (pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are null, amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are null), so POL-RD-05 cannot substitute a re-quoted optimal; and the vehicle type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline has no application. The 10.0 km booked optimal stands as the comparator for the whole trip.

If a deviation were established, the quantum is the rider's own figure rather than an invented one. Running POL-RD-02 on the fare_breakdown, and reading the surge multiplier of 1.0 from that same artifact as POL-RD-02 requires: (3.80 + 0.75 x 10.0 + 0.28 x 20.0) x 1.0 = 16.90, plus the 0.80 platform fee = 17.70; the refund is 19.39 - 17.70 = 1.69, rounded up to 1.70, comfortably above the 0.50 de minimis.

The rider's profile imposes no additional corroboration on this claim: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the POL-RD-08 condition of 4 or more claims with 1 or fewer substantiated is not met and the unimpaired trace measures the excess on its own. No other field on either profile is relied on for any purpose, as POL-GEN-01 requires.

Every dollar the rider paid went into distance and time on the route actually driven. The fare breakdown reconciles line by line — base 3.80 + distance 8.63 + time 6.16 + platform 0.80 = 19.39 — and the 8.63 distance line is the trace's own 11.5 km at 0.75 per km, with no ERP gantry, no toll and no surcharge anywhere in the ledger, so 1.5 km of that billed distance lies beyond the route quoted at booking.

claims.text: The governing distance measurement is the length of the gps_trace polyline, and POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the field that controls the threshold test — trip_record.actual_distance_km is a rounded convenience copy of the same measurement and may not be cited for it. The trace records 11.5 km against a booked optimal of 10.0 km, an excess of 1.50 km, and the platform's own derived block carries that same figure with status 'no deviation'.

POL-RD-01 requires BOTH establishment tests to pass: the excess must be greater than 20% of optimal_distance_km AND greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms. The absolute limb is met at 1.50 km, but the 1.50 km excess is 15.00% of the 10.0 km optimal route, which is under the 20% limb. The percentage test fails, and on POL-RD-01's own wording both must pass.

Because one of the two mandatory establishment tests fails, no route deviation exists on this trip, and POL-RD-01 directs that the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip. The rider's own claim — 'about 1.5 km longer' — is arithmetically the 15% figure that falls below the gate, so his evidence proves the driver's point rather than his own.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and must show an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold before the burden shifts to the driver. He cannot discharge limb (b): 1.50 km on a 10.0 km optimal is 15%, short of the 20% limb. The burden never shifts, so the driver is not required to invoke POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05, POL-RD-11 or POL-RD-12 at all, and the chat log in any event contains no detour instruction — only the rider's single observation that the ride 'looks a little longer'.

The trace cannot be displaced as unreliable: it carries 133 fixes at a 10-second sample interval, 100% coverage, no gaps at all and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds, and its admissibility is COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0 with no issue codes. POL-RD-07's impairment limbs (a) to (c) are therefore not engaged, the measurement stands as recorded, and there is no data failure to escalate on.

POL-RD-02, the optimal-route fare recomputation, runs only 'where a deviation is established under POL-RD-01'. No deviation is established here, so the recomputation never runs, no distance refund is available to the rider, and his request that the difference be refunded has no basis in the policy arithmetic.

There is no residual billing-integrity correction under POL-RD-09(4) that could reach the same result by another route. The fare_breakdown shows an empty erp_gantries array, an airport_surcharge of 0.00 on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport, and distance_charged_km of 11.5 km matching the trace figure exactly — every charged line has a counterpart, so no line is refundable as a standalone pass-through correction.

NO_ACTION is party-relative under POL-GEN-03: it leaves fare_breakdown.payment_status and refund_issued_sgd exactly as they are. This is a rider-filed dispute and the charge is recorded as 'CHARGED' with 0.00 refunded, so NO_ACTION preserves the driver's metered fare of SGD 19.39 in full and moves no money against him.

ruling.explanation: To both parties: this is a route-deviation dispute over a completed trip of 11.5 km against a booked optimal route of 10.0 km — an excess of 1.50 km, or 15% of the optimal distance. POL-RD-01 sets two establishment tests and both must pass: the excess must be greater than 20% of the optimal distance AND greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms. The absolute limb is met (1.50 km), but the percentage limb is not (15% is below 20%). One failed limb means no route deviation exists on this trip, so the distance refund the rider asks for has no basis and POL-RD-02 (the fare recomputation) never runs. The rider's own arithmetic — 1.5 km on a 10.0 km optimal — is the 15% figure that falls below the gate; this is not a criticism of the rider, it is simply what the policy threshold requires. I also checked every alternative route to a refund. The fare breakdown is METERED with surge_multiplier 1.0 read from that artifact; POL-RD-11 (upfront-quoted fares) does not apply. There is no billing-integrity correction under POL-RD-09(4): erp_gantries is empty, the airport surcharge is 0.00 on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport, and the billed distance of 11.5 km matches the trace exactly, so every charged line has a counterpart. POL-RD-05 and POL-RD-12 are unavailable: the trip record shows no relocation (amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are null) and the vehicle type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so the 10.0 km booked optimal is the correct comparator. The GPS trace is unimpaired for policy purposes — 133 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds, admissibility COMPLETE at weight 1.0 — so POL-RD-07 is not engaged and nothing is discounted. The chat log holds a single message from the rider, an observation rather than a detour instruction, and waypoint_hint is null, so POL-RD-04 cannot be run and the driver's assertion that he stayed on ordinary through roads (which cites no artifact) changes nothing under POL-RD-08. The traffic advisory artifact EV-ADVIS-09112-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT; its absence is citable but it exonerates nothing under POL-RD-03 and, under POL-GEN-02, it does not carry the deciding fact and so does not affect confidence. The rider's profile imposes no extra corroboration (deviation_claims_60d is 0). As no deviation is established and no charge line is defective, the outcome is NO_ACTION: the metered fare of SGD 19.39 stays charged and the refund remains SGD 0.00, exactly as the record stands.

To both parties: this case turns on the route-deviation threshold in POL-RD-01, and it does not clear it. The completed trip measured 11.5 km on the GPS trace against a booked optimal of 10.0 km, so the excess is 1.5 km. POL-RD-01 requires BOTH establishment tests to pass: the excess must be greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms AND greater than 20% of the optimal distance. The 1.5 km clears the absolute limb, but 1.5 km is only 15% of the 10.0 km optimal route, which is below the 20% limb. Because both tests must pass together and one fails, no route deviation is established and the rider's request for a distance refund cannot be granted. The rider's own arithmetic in fact demonstrates this: the 1.5 km he reports is the same 15% figure that falls short of the gate. The driver's point on this is accepted, and the trace (133 fixes, 10-second sampling, 100% coverage, no gaps, unimpaired under POL-RD-07 and weighted 1.0) is the governing measurement under POL-RD-01. On the rider's side, the conditional fare recomputation under POL-RD-02 (which would produce 19.39 - 17.70 = 1.69, rounded to 1.70) never runs, because POL-RD-02 applies only 'where a deviation is established under POL-RD-01', and none is. That conditional claim is therefore inapplicable to this trip. The chat log contains a single message from the rider - 'This looks a little longer than the route shown at booking' - which is a question, not an instruction; it names no road or place and waypoint_hint is null, so the POL-RD-04 corroboration test cannot be run and that clause exonerates nothing either way. No re-baselining applies: the trip record shows no pickup or dropoff amendment, and the vehicle is RYDE_X rather than RYDE_POOL, so the 10.0 km booked optimal stands as the comparator. There is no billing-integrity correction under POL-RD-09(4): the fare breakdown shows no ERP gantries, no airport surcharge on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport, and a distance charge of 11.5 km that matches the trace exactly, so every charged line has a counterpart. The one missing artifact, the traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-09112-01, MISSING, weight 0.0), is noted and would carry no fact, but its absence is irrelevant here because no deviation exists to be exonerated and no party asserted a closure. The rider's profile adds no corroboration requirement (deviation_claims_60d is 0). No escalation trigger under POL-RD-10 fires and no clause produces a referral. Outcome: NO_ACTION. The metered fare of SGD 19.39 stands and fare_breakdown.payment_status and refund_issued_sgd are left as they are.

Ruling for both parties — route deviation dispute, trip TRP-09112, 19 Sep 2026.

THE DECIDING ARITHMETIC. POL-RD-01 establishes a route deviation only when the excess over the booked optimal route is greater than 20% of that optimal AND greater than 0.8 km, and it says in terms that both tests must pass. The governing distance is the GPS polyline (gps_trace.trace_distance_km = 11.5 km), not the trip record's rounded copy; both happen to read 11.5 km here. Against the booked optimal of 10.0 km the excess is 1.5 km. That clears the 0.8 km limb but is only 15.0% of the optimal, below the 20% limb. One of two mandatory tests fails, so no deviation is ESTABLISHED and the outcome is NO_ACTION.

TO THE RIDER. Your own figure — 'about 1.5 km longer' — is the 15% number, and the platform's derived block records status 'no deviation' on the same figures. The SGD 1.69 you arrive at is the correct POL-RD-02 arithmetic on this fare, but POL-RD-02 runs only 'where a deviation is established under POL-RD-01'. It is not established, so that computation never runs and the distance difference is not refundable. Your point that 1.5 km of the billed distance lies beyond the route quoted at booking is accurate, but 1.5 km on a 10.0 km route is deliberately under the refundable gate the policy sets.

TO THE DRIVER. Your metered fare stands. You did not need to invoke any exculpatory clause: because the POL-RD-08 burden of proof never shifts to you (the rider could not show an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold), POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05, POL-RD-11 and POL-RD-12 are not engaged. Your counterparty statement ('I stayed on ordinary through roads and made no additional stop') cites no evidence ID, so under POL-RD-08 it carries no weight; nothing in this ruling turns on it either way.

EVIDENCE QUALITY. The GPS trace is unimpaired for policy purposes: 133 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps, maximum gap 0.0 s, admissibility COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0 with no issue codes. None of POL-RD-07 limbs (a)–(c) is engaged, so there is no data failure to escalate on. The only impaired artifact in the bundle, the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-09112-01, is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT); it carries no fact, no party asserted a road closure, and its absence cannot exculpate anyone, so POL-RD-03 exonerates nothing and POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged. POL-RD-10 is not triggered on any limb: identifiers match (TRP-09112 throughout), the timestamps are consistent (driver arrival at pickup 14:09, trip start 14:10, end 14:32, ledger 14:32:03), confidence is above the 0.70 floor, and no line of the fare lacks a counterpart.

BILLING INTEGRITY. Checked, and there is nothing to correct. The ledger reconciles line by line — base 3.80 + distance 8.63 (11.5 km x 0.75) + time 6.16 (22 min x 0.28) + platform 0.80 = 19.39 — with an empty ERP gantry array, no tolls and a 0.00 airport surcharge on a trip that neither starts nor ends at an airport. POL-RD-09(4) produces no standalone refund.

PROFILES. Neither profile is used as a ground of decision. The rider's deviation_claims_60d (0) and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated (0) are the only profile fields either side cited, they are citable under POL-RD-08, and they do not trigger the extra-corroboration condition. No context-only field (rating, account age, lifetime trips, cancellation rate, prior counters) was relied on. Because the deciding fact is carried by two independent artifacts each at weight 1.0 (the GPS trace and the trip record — one measuring the distance driven, the other the booked optimal), the confidence cap is 1.0.

OUTCOME. NO_ACTION. Under POL-GEN-03 this is party-relative: this is a rider-filed dispute and the charge stays exactly as recorded — payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00, the driver's SGD 19.39 metered fare preserved. No money moves, no compensation is owed, and no clause produces a referral.

The percentage limb is not met on this record, and the rider does not assert that a route deviation is established by the 1.5 km excess.
